text: Synchrony Bank intentionally uses misleading wording on their online auto-pay to trick consumers into their pay in full option, enabling increased interest/investment profit for their XXXXwo week " standard '' reimbursement period ( 10 business day ). While all Synchrony statements are " monthly statements, '' they use the term " statement balance '' in exchange for " pay in full. '' As the bulk of their business model is built around retail financing for " 0 % interest for X months '' promotions, in which the monthly " statement balance '' should be the total account balance divided by the number of months financed, the " statement balance '' option should only deduct this amount as consumers expect that their options are to pay the monthly statement balance to pay the account off within the 0 % interest period, to pay more than the statement balance to pay the account off early, or pay less than the statement balance at the risk of paying interest. However, in an effort to fabricate additional capital at the expense of the consumers, they have created their own nomenclature to promote errant registration to forego the agreed to 0 % interest period in exchange for their " pay in full '' interest income scheme. I had signed up for 0 % interest for 24 months promotion through XXXX XXXX, and then when I set up my online auto-pay through the Synchrony website, selecting to pay the monthly statement balance, they withdrew the full loan amount from my checking account, incurring an overdraft, and then said that they could not reverse the charge but would send me a check in 10 business days. I spoke to mulitiple people with customer service, and was instructed that they were unwilling to reverse the charge immediately and would only send out a check. Using this scheme, the company is able to trick consumers and hold their money for additional interest/investment income.
